subject: Transportation Systems
title: How Wings Create Lift
description: A quick win: understand How Wings Create Lift.

hook.text: A 747 weighs 400 tons. Yet it flies because of a simple trick air plays over curved surfaces.

buildup.text: A wing's top surface is curved more than the bottom. Air moves faster over the top.

discovery.text: Faster air creates lower pressure above the wing. Higher pressure below pushes the wing up. That's lift.

twist.text: This alone doesn't explain everything. The wing also deflects air downward—Newton's third law helps too.

climax.text: Lift is a partnership: pressure difference and air deflection working together.

punchline.text: Wings don't defy gravity. They redirect air.

quiz.question: What creates lift on an airplane wing?
options: Hot air rising from the engine
